analysis.investment_thesis: Crizac is an exceptional capital-light business (ROCE 48%) that compounds at high rates — exactly the quality the Magic Formula rewards — but at INR 230, the earnings yield of ~5.4% (EBIT 213 Cr / EV ~3,939 Cr) sits below my 6% threshold, meaning the market has already priced in the quality. A great business at a full price is a hold, not a buy.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROCE of 48% and ROE of 36% — capital-light consultancy model with near-zero capex (INR 1 Cr in 2025) means almost all EBIT flows to returns
Zero debt, INR 89 Cr cash, and 4/4 years of positive OCF (INR 187 Cr in 2025) — fortress balance sheet
Revenue CAGR of 66.3% (2021–2025) with operating income growing even faster at 67.6% — scale without margin dilution
key_risks: Earnings yield ~5.4% (EBIT/EV) is below my 6% minimum — limited margin of safety at current price for Magic Formula buyers
Other income (INR 35 Cr in 2025, INR 53 Cr in 2024) contributes ~23% of net profit — likely investment income from IPO proceeds; strips out, core earnings quality needs scrutiny
Anomalous INR 119 Cr capex in FY2024 (vs INR 1 Cr in all other years) is unexplained and turned FCF negative that year — capital allocation discipline unclear
red_flags: Other income is 23% of net profit — overstates true operating earnings power
FY2024 capex spike of INR 119 Cr with no CWIP build-up is a data inconsistency worth investigating
Promoter holding of 79.94% leaves very thin float; FII/DII at only 2.48%/3.48% signals limited institutional validation so far
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Using the Magic Formula, Crizac scores well on one leg but fails the other. Return on Capital is outstanding — ROCE of 48% on a near-zero fixed-asset base (capex INR 1 Cr in 2025) confirms this is a genuinely high-quality franchise aggregating student placements into UK/Canada/Australia universities. The EBITDA CAGR of 72.7% over four years shows the business model scales with minimal incremental capital, which is exactly the profile I prize. However, on Earnings Yield — the other leg of my formula — EBIT of INR 213 Cr against an EV of roughly INR 3,939 Cr (market cap INR 4,028 Cr less INR 89 Cr cash) produces a yield of only ~5.4%, below my 6% floor and far below the 12%+ I find compelling. The market has priced in the quality fully.

Two items need deeper diligence before upgrading. First, other income (INR 35–53 Cr in recent years) appears to be returns on a large investment portfolio built from IPO proceeds — strip this out and the P/E on core operating earnings is meaningfully higher than the headline 20.8x. Second, the INR 119 Cr capex in FY2024 with zero CWIP accumulation and no explanatory disclosure is a flag worth probing in annual reports. At forward P/E of 16x the stock could re-rate as earnings grow into the valuation, but for the Magic Formula to trigger a buy signal I'd need the price to correct ~25-30% to push earnings yield above 7%.
